issues.legal_issue: A secured creditor may realise its security outside a company’s winding up without leave of the winding-up court, and a sale made without the court’s intervention is not void merely because leave was not obtained.
material_facts: The company was in winding up and its debenture trustees held security over its assets.
The trustees’ receiver, acting under the security, sold company assets after the winding-up order without seeking leave of the winding-up court or using the court’s process.
The sale was challenged as void under the provision governing sales made without the court’s leave during winding up.
issues.conclusion: The sale was valid and binding; the statutory reference to a sale made without leave applies to sales through the intervention of the court, not a secured creditor’s sale outside the winding up.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 171, 229 and 232(1) of the Indian Companies Act, a secured creditor remains outside the winding up when realising its security without the court’s intervention, although leave is required to bring or pursue legal proceedings against the company. The words concerning a sale in section 232(1), read alongside attachment, distress and execution, refer to court-mediated sales. The court applied the contextual construction principle expressed in noscitur a sociis and Angus Robertson v. George Day, and the presumption against implied alteration of law, supported by Murugian v. Jainudeen, National Assistance Board v. Wilkinson and Vasudeva Mudaliar v. Srinivasa Pillai. It also relied on Food Controller v. Cork and The Governor-General in Council v. Shiromani Sugar Mills Ltd. for the secured creditor’s position outside the winding up, and considered Kayastha Trading and Banking Corporation Ltd. v. Sat Narain Singh and Baldeo Narain Singh v. The United India Bank Ltd. in explaining the purpose of the amendment.

predicates.company_in_winding_up: The company whose assets are involved is being wound up.
predicates.secured_creditor_realizes_security: A creditor holding security over the company’s property acts to realise that security.
predicates.sale_without_court_intervention: The secured creditor sells the property outside the winding-up court’s process.

issues.definition: When a company is being wound up and a secured creditor sells its security outside the court’s process, the sale does not require leave of the winding-up court.

issues.legal_issue: A bona fide sale of secured assets outside a company’s winding up cannot be set aside for inadequate publicity or undervalue in the absence of fraud or recklessness.
material_facts: The receiver advertised the intended sale, but the High Court found that the publicity was inadequate.
The courts below found that the accepted offer was the best price available in the circumstances.
The receiver’s bona fides were not challenged, and no fraud or recklessness in making the sale was alleged.
The sale was challenged in proceedings seeking to set it aside.
issues.conclusion: The sale could not be avoided on the grounds of inadequate publicity or undervalue in the circumstances of the case.
issues.legal_principle: The court accepted the conclusion that, where a secured creditor realises its security outside the winding up and there is no allegation of want of bona fides, recklessness or fraud, the sale is not avoided merely because of inadequate notice or undervalue. The court relied on the concurrent findings that the sale was bona fide and obtained the best price available, and on the secured creditor’s right to realise its security outside the winding up as explained in Food Controller v. Cork.

rule.if: proceeding_seeks_to_set_aside_secured_sale and secured_sale_outside_winding_up and bona_fide_sale and best_price_available and no_fraud_or_recklessness_alleged

predicates.proceeding_seeks_to_set_aside_secured_sa: A proceeding seeks to set aside a sale made by a secured creditor.
predicates.secured_sale_outside_winding_up: The secured creditor sells the property outside the company’s winding-up process.
predicates.bona_fide_sale: The sale was made bona fide.
predicates.best_price_available: The accepted offer was found to be the best price available in the circumstances.
predicates.no_fraud_or_recklessness_alleged: No fraud or recklessness in making the sale was alleged.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks to set aside a bona fide secured sale made outside winding up, the best available price was obtained, and fraud or recklessness was not alleged, the sale is not avoided for inadequate publicity or undervalue.
